channel.title: Donetsk 2011 · updates
channel.description: Every change to the Donetsk 2011 game, site and research.

item.title: Site · v3.9 · Day and night on Donetsk time, “Then and later”, a sound diary
item.description:
The site now lives on Donetsk time: when it is night in Donetsk, the album goes dark. New: a “How to help” page, a sound diary and four places in the city before and after 2014.

New

  • A “now in Donetsk” clock in the menu and day and night that follow the sun over the city
  • “Then and later”: four places before and after 2014 with a time slider
  • A “How to help” page: photos, memories, the game, a link for friends
  • A “Sound diary”: a cassette player for future recordings and themes, made without AI

Improved

  • The theme button has three modes: Donetsk time, light and dark
  • Pages turn slightly warmer at dawn and dusk

item.title: Site · v3.8 · Site guests, RSS and a living album
item.description:
The site now has guests: you can see how many times people came here and from which countries. Updates can be followed via RSS, and the album pages came to life.

New

  • “Guests of Donetsk 2011” on the home page: the visit count and stamps with country flags
  • An RSS feed of updates in four languages and a “Follow the project” button
  • Preview cards for each section when you hover the menu
  • The “five pillars” hang on a string and flutter like a paper flag

Improved

  • The page under the cursor is loaded in advance, so navigation is almost instant
  • Buttons fill with colour like ink, and a second photo peeks out from behind the section cards
  • Wikimedia Commons photos are gradually moving onto the site itself: faster and more reliable

item.title: Site · v3.6 · A new look: a family photo album from 2011
item.description:
The site no longer looks like a tech template. It now feels like an album you leaf through at home: paper, white-bordered prints, handwritten captions and the orange date of a digital camera on the photos.

New

  • Alegreya for headings, Literata for text, handwritten Caveat for captions
  • Archive photos, Unreal frames and previews as taped prints
  • The author’s story is laid out as a letter instead of a dark slide
  • The dark theme is now an album under a lamp, without the cold blue

Improved

  • Project figures and milestones are written in the margins instead of grey tiles

item.title: Site · v3.5 · A Donetsk quiz: 53 photos, a city map and a photo of the day
item.description:
The small 14-photo guessing game is now a full quiz: 53 photos from 2008–2013 of 19 places in the city and four modes.

New

  • Where on the map?: put a pin on the map of Donetsk, points depend on the distance
  • Guess the year: taken before 2011, in 2011 or later
  • Photo of the day: one photo for everyone, one try and a result in squares for Telegram and Instagram
  • Shared stats: each photo shows how many players got it right
  • Readers’ photos: your own 2008–2012 shots can be sent by email, and the best go into the quiz and the archive

Improved

  • Guess the place: 19 places instead of 7, from the railway station and the airport to the slag heaps
  • A new map of the whole city from OpenStreetMap: roads, rivers, ponds, parks

item.title: Site · v3.4 · Before/after, a live preview and memories without GitHub
item.description:
The site shows more: blockout progress is visible with a slider, the home page plays a live model of the quarter, and a memory can now be sent as an ordinary email.

New

  • A before/after comparison on the Development page and in the updates feed
  • A live video of the 3D quarter on the home page that opens the model in one click
  • Memory map: sending by email without an account, fields for text and signature
  • Guess the place: after answering you can add a memory of that place straight away

Improved

  • The home video is 0.6 MB, loads only when visible and does not play with data saver or reduced motion
  • The Contact section on the Press page: the author’s email

item.title: Site · v3.3 · Press kit and faster loading
item.description:
The site got lighter and easier to share: moving between pages is several times faster and links now show proper previews.

New

  • A Press page: description, facts, images and a logo
  • Link previews for Telegram, Instagram and social networks on every page
  • A custom 404 page

Improved

  • Shared styles and scripts are cached: moving between pages loads 12–35 times less
  • 3D quarter data loads only on Reconstruction
  • A sitemap and structured data for search engines

item.title: Site · v3.1 · The update feed
item.description:
A new page gathers every change to the game, the site and the research into one feed.

New

  • Filter by game, site or research
  • “New” marks since your last visit and a counter in the menu
  • A stage rail: where the project is now
  • A link to every entry and a latest-update card on the home page

item.title: Game · AP-01 · The northern road and the gate from the 2011 panoramas
item.description:
The northern road and the house 33 gate were checked against the October 2011 panoramas: planting on the east verge, scalloped concrete panels, sheet metal turning to brick at label 27. DX11: 27 surface checks, 3 routes, 22 captures.

New

  • 7 trees, 10 shrubs and a low wall on the east verge
  • Scalloped concrete gate panels with relief joints
  • A low board fence north of label 30

Improved

  • A soft dirt-to-asphalt edge at the gate
  • Shrubs and a tree on the west verge

item.title: Site · v3.0 · The real Donetsk and a model of the quarter
item.description:
Grey captures gave way to photographs of the city from 2008–2013 and renders of the 3D model lit by the October 2011 sun.

New

  • A 22-photo archive with filters and a full-screen viewer
  • The 3D quarter with shadows and a sun slider set to 15 October 2011
  • A walk through the 3D model with Back and Next buttons
  • “Guess the place”: 14 photos, 7 places and a best score

Improved

  • A hero image of Donetsk at dusk in November 2011
  • Development in order: goal, method, engine, blockout, plan, log
  • Unreal captures gathered in the Blockout section

Fixed

  • Removed the link to the deleted atlas

item.title: Site · v2.1 · Comfortable on a phone
item.description:
The mobile version got a pinned menu and tidier typography.

New

  • The ☰ menu is pinned to the top of the screen

Improved

  • The log shows the last 4 entries on phones
  • Headings scale to fit the screen width

Fixed

  • Long words no longer break in the middle
  • Pages no longer slide sideways on narrow screens

item.title: Site · v2.0 · Four pages instead of one
item.description:
The site is split into Home, The city, Reconstruction and Development. Each page answers its own question.

New

  • A page menu and quick links to sections

Improved

  • The gist of the atlas moved into the memory map caption

Fixed

  • Removed repeated blocks

item.title: Game · AP-01 · Planting before the northern building
item.description: The October 2011 south view showed dense greenery on the west verge. The model now has four shrubs and a small tree there; the full DX11 run passed 27 checks and 3 routes.

item.title: Game · AP-01 · The north of the quarter and the first 67 metres
item.description:
The north of the quarter: a retaining wall with a lawn and conifers, end-wall windows and a service court without the misplaced annex. The first 67 m of the street got trees, shrubs, dirt shoulders and separate surfaces.

New

  • A retaining wall, a raised lawn and three conifers
  • Windows and projecting edges on the end facade
  • 7 trees, 7 shrubs and 4 garden clusters on the first segment

Improved

  • Asphalt, patches, dirt and gravel are now separate surfaces

Fixed

  • Removed a misplaced annex that blocked the service lane

item.title: Site · v1.4 · The memory map
item.description:
Anyone who remembers Donetsk can mark a place on the map and leave a memory.

New

  • A 4.37 × 2.84 km map of the centre where you pick a point
  • Submission through a GitHub form with the place's coordinates
  • The memory appears on the site after review

item.title: Site · v1.3 · The 3D quarter, a walk and a game
item.description:
The site became interactive: you can fly over the quarter, walk the street and remember the city in a game.

New

  • A 280 × 660 m 3D model of the quarter right in the browser
  • Evidence mode: every house shows what is known and what is estimated
  • A walk down Zarichna through 9 panorama points from 2011
  • The “Guess the place” game and the sound diary shelf

Improved

  • “New” marks in the development log

item.title: Game · AP-01 · An observation walk in the game
item.description:
The playable quarter now starts at house 33 and guides the player through six October 2011 panorama points. The HUD shows what is known and what is estimated.

New

  • Six steps through the 2011 panorama points
  • A restrained HUD without money or missions

Improved

  • The crowd walks only along the east verge of the quarter
  • A tool for repeatable drive-through captures

item.title: Game · AP-01 · The working quarter of Zarichna and Donetska
item.description:
A working Zarichna and Donetska quarter, 280 × 660 m: 189 volumes, SRTM terrain and a continuous 412 m corridor based on six October 2011 panoramas. 18 surface checks, ≈ 564 m routes along each street and 38 GIS tests passed.

New

  • 189 volumes from individual OSM outlines
  • SRTM terrain under the whole quarter
  • A continuous 412 m corridor from six panoramas

Improved

  • 18 surface checks and 38 GIS tests

item.title: Research · M01 · Checking OSM from 2012
item.description: OSM in 2012 compared with today's map: 91 candidates, 18 reviewed. None entered the 2011 canon without dated imagery.

item.title: Site · v1.2 · Why the city is out of reach
item.description:
The home page gained Davito Daveeni's 2012 film about Donetsk and figures with sources.

New

  • A section on why there is no way back to Donetsk
  • The 2012 documentary with thanks to its author

Improved

  • Every figure checked and sourced

item.title: Game · AP-01 · The first Windows player
item.description:
The first Windows player with a pause menu, saving and loading. A 54 m frontage study near no. 33 and eight frames captured straight from Unreal.

New

  • Pause menu, saving and loading
  • A 54 m facade study at house 33

item.title: Site · v1.0 · The site goes live
item.description:
Project website launched in four languages.

New

  • Russian, Ukrainian, English and Finnish
  • A personal story and Street View panoramas from 2011
  • A photo archive of Donetsk before 2014
  • A live Donetsk 2011 clock and a ticker of streets

item.title: Game · M02 · Moving to Unreal Engine 5.8
item.description: Move to Unreal Engine 5.8.3: the Development Editor build succeeded and the game launched on DX11. Decision DEC-0001: I start the First Playable while research continues in parallel.

item.title: Game · P0 · The Unity prototype
item.description: Unity prototype: 6 routes over 1,200 m, 1,002 ground samples, Windows and Android test builds.

item.title: Research · M01 · The October 2011 panoramas
item.description: October 2011 Street View panoramas walked along Zarichna Street in both directions. The audit of 126 footprints found no overlaps.

item.title: Research · M01 · The origin point
item.description: Origin confirmed: 33 Zarichna St, 47.9927461 N, 37.8183736 E.

item.title: Research · M01 · The reference map of the centre
item.description: OpenStreetMap snapshot: 8,508 elements, a 4.37 × 2.84 km reference map of the centre.
